# OpenIE Research

> Research by David Charlot at Open Interface Engineering, Inc., published free so that anyone can read, reproduce and reuse it. Each paper stands alone, defines its own terms, and opens with three plain-language points. Energy figures are labeled as estimates, operating-system or on-chip readings, or external-meter measurements.

## Research papers

- [Thermodynamic Bounds and an Optimal Tempo for Goal-Holding Agents](https://research.openie.dev/papers/agency/): Defines an agent as a system that holds a goal under an energy budget, derives physical bounds on how fast it can act per second and per joule, and reads intelligence as progress per joule on a completed run. Plain words: to count as an agent, a system must aim at a goal, act, and stay within an energy budget; physics sets a minimum energy cost for every decision; among systems that finish a job correctly, the one that used less energy ranks higher. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/agency.pdf)
- [Metered Commit Gates: Energy-to-Correct-Completion for Agentic Systems](https://research.openie.dev/papers/gates/): A gate that lets a machine act only after a check passes, and a cascade that tries the cheapest method first, with software results and one board-level energy reading (11,428 pJ per gate cycle, whole module, KV260). Plain words: do not take an action that cannot be undone until a check says it is safe; try the cheapest way first; write every decision down with its energy. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/gates.pdf)
- [The Reality Code Engine: One Lossless Form for Native, Verified, Low-Energy Programming](https://research.openie.dev/papers/rce/): A system in which a program is written once as a state machine and code in other languages is generated from it, with measurements on 10,000 Forms and public bug datasets and falsifiers fixed in advance. Plain words: write a program once and generate it in many languages; reject broken input at the door; save checked fixes so the same problem is not paid for twice. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/rce.pdf)
- [The Pursuit of AGI Resolves the Three-Body Problem in Computing](https://research.openie.dev/papers/three-body/): Locates many computing failures at handoffs between the people who specify, build and use systems, states when checking every handoff assumption makes a stack stable, and supports it with independently tested verified systems (CompCert, seL4, TLA+ at AWS, unit types). Plain words: most big failures happen at handoffs; the cause is usually an unwritten guess; if every guess is written down and machine-checked, a fix stays fixed. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/three-body.pdf)

## Economics papers and essays

- [Task Satiation vs. Aggregate Rebound in AI Demand](https://research.openie.dev/papers/satiation/): Defines the stop at which more machine work on a finished task adds nothing, and separates it from growth in total demand. Plain words: every job has a finish line; cheaper work can still create more jobs; AI prices fall but its electricity is never free. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/satiation.pdf)
- [Spell Check is Global: The Future of Computer Intelligence in the Hands of the Many (7B+), Not the Few](https://research.openie.dev/papers/spellcheck/): Documents with dated prices how spell check went from a premium product to a free built-in feature, and explains it by marginal cost and bundling. Plain words: spell check used to cost a lot and is now free; it became free because it costs almost nothing to run and is most useful inside tools people have; other computer skills can follow. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/spellcheck.pdf)
- [The Promised Trillion Dollar AI-Coding Market](https://research.openie.dev/papers/ai-coding-market/): Lists who projects a trillion-dollar AI coding market, labels each number by kind, and names the shared assumptions about energy, tokens and reuse, with testable propositions. Plain words: the big numbers are mostly forecasts; they assume a large model is paid for every piece of code forever; reuse would lower the cost of repeated work toward the cost of electricity. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/ai-coding-market.pdf)
- [The Price of the Unexamined Interface](https://research.openie.dev/papers/interface-economics/): Published costs of failures at handoffs, labeled as accounted costs, model estimates or survey estimates and never added into one total. Plain words: some handoff failures have exact price tags; national totals are estimates; checking assumptions is cheap but the one who does it pays while everyone benefits. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/interface-economics.pdf)
- [The Gap Between Possible and Deployed: A Cadence Model of Computer Intelligence and the Forcing Function of Automation Tools](https://research.openie.dev/papers/latency/): Public methods that lower the cost of computer intelligence reach products after a delay with technical, calendar and incentive parts, modeled with six propositions and six refutable predictions. Plain words: cheaper methods are published long before products use them; part of the wait is calendars; once work is cheap, what remains to charge for is the cost of switching away.

## White papers

- [Metabolic Intelligence: Budget-Native Compute from Tag to Campus](https://research.openie.dev/products/mei/): Computer intelligence designed to run inside a fixed energy budget, with emulator and datasheet results on a cold-chain sensor tag and a protocol test of a grid-following data center. Plain words: give a computer a fixed energy budget and design it for the best answer inside it; a food sensor tag can then run about eight years on a coin battery; a data center can cut power when the grid asks without giving wrong answers. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/mei.pdf)
- [The Search for JouleOS](https://research.openie.dev/products/jouleos/): A review of how operating systems, instruction sets and agent sandboxes are composed today, and checkable requirements for a machine that schedules, meters and refuses an agent under an energy budget. Plain words: AI agents are added on top of old layers; none of them checks energy before an agent acts; a machine for agents should measure energy, budget it, and refuse what breaks the budget. [PDF](https://research.openie.dev/pdfs/jouleos.pdf)

## Earlier addresses

- /papers/ni/ and /papers/mol/ open the matching part of [Metered Commit Gates](https://research.openie.dev/papers/gates/), with section anchors. /papers/mei/ and /papers/jouleos/ open the product white papers under /products/.

## Reference

- [Glossary](https://research.openie.dev/glossary/): Terms used on the site. Each paper also defines its own terms.
- [About the papers](https://research.openie.dev/about/): One page per paper on what it claims and what it does not.
- [Figures](https://research.openie.dev/living/): Interactive figures for the papers.
- [RCE Playground](https://openie-dev.github.io/rce/): the reference checker (checker-wasm) in the browser: write, check and run RCE programs, with the specification examples and shareable links.
- [RCE engine demo](https://research.openie.dev/demos/rce-engine/): Browser-only demo running the RCE core compiled to WebAssembly, with no server and no model calls. Layers cover code, the state machine view, proof replay, interface checks, compounding, energy estimates, held-out results and translation to Rust, Python, XState and SCXML.

## Optional

- [OpenIE](https://openie.dev/): Open Interface Engineering, Inc., publisher of this site.

## Translations

Each paper has translated editions, marked as translations of the English version, which prevails. Pages with only a translated title and abstract say so and link the English full text. URL pattern: https://research.openie.dev/<lang>/papers/<slug>/ with lang in zh-Hans (Chinese (Simplified)), es (Spanish), fr (French), de (German), ja (Japanese), pt (Portuguese), hi (Hindi), ar (Arabic). Example: https://research.openie.dev/ja/papers/rce/
